phone_ban.why: X captures realistic second-round effects (foreign makers repricing below the cap, later FX shock, customs revenue recovering via quota). Y is numerically tighter but has a static environment and end-of-game artifacts (stockpiling or expanding because it is the last stage).

free_coder.why: X shows a turning point: a downturn on top of free AI leads to contract cuts, layoffs and emigration, then a niche for complex and review work. Y is a smooth, shock-free glide where developers upskill every stage and employment barely moves.

water_ration.why: X stress-tests the plan with rumour, heat, a pipe burst and rain, and shows anger peaking when the tariff hike coincides with the burst. Y has no events at all, flat health risk, and tanker hikes driven by last-stage logic.

truck_strike.why: Y shows escalation (panic buying, blockades, ports), shelf depletion and prices staying high after the deal. X keeps shelves full throughout a nationwide strike, settles within days, and then has two empty stages where every actor holds.
